title: Resurfacing after the water mains settle

blocks.text: A city's public works department schedules water-main replacements and street resurfacing for 2027 to 2033. The model in `streets.py` has a binary `x[pid, t]` for each project and each year `t` in its `starts`; each project starts at most once (given). A water main takes `duration` years of work: one started in 2028 with a duration of 2 is dug up through 2029.

`after` maps a resurfacing project to a pair `(main, settle)`. The rule: a street may be resurfaced only after the water main under it is finished, and only once the trench has settled for `settle` full years. With the main above and `settle = 1`, 2030 is the settling year, and the street may be resurfaced in 2031 or later. A resurfacing project whose main is not funded may not be done at all. A resurfacing project that is not in `after` has no such rule.
Write `add_after_rules(model, x, projects, after)` so that the model allows exactly the plans that keep the rule.
The model so far, with $`P`$ the projects, $`T_i`$ project $`i`$'s start years and $`d_i`$ its duration:

First turn the rule into a least number of years between the two *starts*, and check it on the example above. Then write one row per resurfacing project and year, with its quantifier and a label, before you code it.
The tests fix every `x[pid, t]` through its bounds and ask the solver whether the model accepts the plan, so any correct formulation passes. About eight lines.

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass

from ortools.math_opt.python import mathopt


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Project:
    pid: str
    starts: tuple[int, ...]
    duration: int = 1


def add_after_rules(model: mathopt.Model, x: dict, projects: list[Project],
                    after: dict[str, tuple[str, int]]) -> None:
    """Each resurfacing starts only once its water main is finished and the trench has settled."""
    # TODO: one row per resurfacing project and year.
    return None


def build(projects: list[Project], after: dict[str, tuple[str, int]]) -> tuple[mathopt.Model, dict]:
    model = mathopt.Model(name="streets")
    x = {(p.pid, t): model.add_binary_variable(name=f"x_{p.pid}_{t}") for p in projects for t in p.starts}
    for p in projects:
        model.add_linear_constraint(sum(x[p.pid, t] for t in p.starts) <= 1, name=f"once_{p.pid}")
    add_after_rules(model, x, projects, after)
    return model, x


if __name__ == "__main__":
    projects = [Project("MAIN", (2027, 2028), 2), Project("PAVE", (2029, 2030, 2031))]
    model, x = build(projects, {"PAVE": ("MAIN", 1)})
    print(model.get_num_linear_constraints(), "rows")

cases.says: resurfacing well after its water main is allowed, and resurfacing with no water main is refused
a street with no water main under it may be resurfaced in any of its years
resurfacing while the water main is still being dug is refused
resurfacing in the year right after the water main finishes is refused when the ground must settle a year
resurfacing as soon as the settling time is over is allowed
